features.summary: A handler and the run it starts: the view's trigger door, on load once its owner has started, a pipeline whose steps run in the trigger's turn until one waits, two handlers of one event in the order they subscribed, and the handler's policy over a run still in flight.

meanings.meaning: On load runs once per start of its owner, after every handler that start subscribes has subscribed: at boot, every handler of every plan the page holds, a server-rendered slot's included; at a slot's load, every handler of the plans that load starts. The on-load handlers then run in D17.3's subscription order, so an on-load's dispatch reaches every handler its start subscribed and every handler the page subscribed before it. Neither line's on load carries a payload, so its handler's payload path is []. The plan carries on load as the redesign does (Alis.Reactive/PlanAuthoring/Pipelines/TriggerBuilder.cs:31-34, Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Writing/Scope.cs:175 and Alis.Reactive/PlanModel/Writing/Scope.cs:205 at 65fdf118d), which the schema changes in nothing: a handler of the event ready on the document plugin's object, $document, a plugin locator of alis.document with an empty key and data none, whose listening is an EventTarget's (D17.14); the handler's members are required and its policy is overlap, since it runs once per start of its owner and its door takes none (N11.1).

features.oracle: The spec itself, where the framework is the authority: Run.tla and Lanes.tla for a run, its order and its policy; and the DOM Standard's event dispatch, which calls an event's listeners in the order they were added.

defects.defect: An on-load handler runs before a handler its start subscribes, so its dispatch is lost: a page's on load that dispatches an event a later plan of the page handles, and a slot's on load that dispatches an event its own plan and the page handle (M1.D1).

promises.page: A nurse call button with two handlers of its click: the first sets the call's text from Idle to Heard, awaits the dose scanner's Settle(), which awaits the test app's settle endpoint the harness gates (Run.tla's Settle), then sets the desk's text from Waiting to Acknowledged; the second copies the call's text into the empty pager.
promises.gesture: Click the call button, then release the settle once the harness reports it held.
promises.outcome: Before the release the pager reads Heard and the desk reads Waiting; after it the desk reads Acknowledged.
promises.opposite: With the second handler subscribed first, the pager copies Idle.
promises.defect: The second handler waits for the first one's await, so the pager stays empty before the release, or the first never goes on and the desk keeps Waiting.

promises.page: The care panel, the resident record's ConformanceComponent, whose Raise button raises Raised from its own code and, as soon as its listeners return, shows its payload line, Payload text: and the payload's WriteOnlyText, and its answer line, the payload's Answer for its first item, One; two handlers of Raised, neither with an awaited step: the first writes Kappa into the payload's WriteOnlyText, the second sets the payload's Answer to item => pipeline.Concat(item.Name, " by Lambda").
promises.outcome: The panel shows Payload text: Kappa and One by Lambda.
promises.opposite: With the second handler left out, the panel shows Payload text: Kappa and One unanswered.
promises.defect: A handler continues in a microtask, so the panel reads before either write and shows Payload text: none and One unanswered, or the second handler starts after the panel's turn and the answer line reads One unanswered.

promises.page: A ward list whose change handler, under replace, loads the ward's rooms into a room list. The harness gates East's rooms GET (Lanes.tla's Respond).
promises.gesture: Pick ward East; once the harness reports East's GET held, pick ward West and wait until the room list shows West's rooms; then release East's GET.
promises.outcome: The room list still shows West's rooms after East's release.
promises.opposite: Under overlap, the room list shows East's rooms after East's release.
promises.defect: The first run is not cut, so East's late answer overwrites West's rooms.

promises.page: The admission screen's chart save button, whose handler, under skip, posts the chart. The harness gates the POST (Lanes.tla's Respond) and counts the posts the endpoint received.
promises.gesture: Click save; once the harness reports the POST held, click save again, then release it.
promises.outcome: The harness counts one post, and the status reads Saved once.
promises.opposite: A click after the release sends a second post.
promises.defect: The second click starts a run while the first is in flight, so the server receives two posts.

promises.page: A bell whose click handler, under replace, logs rang and its round, sends a request whose route rings the bell again on round 1 and whose Finally logs finally and the round, then logs after and the round.
promises.outcome: The log reads rang 1 finally 1 rang 2 finally 2 after 2.
promises.opposite: Under overlap the log reads rang 1 rang 2 finally 1 after 1 finally 2 after 2.
promises.defect: The new run starts before the old Finally, so the log reads rang 1 rang 2 finally 1, or the old run's after-step runs.

promises.page: A page with two plans: the first's on load dispatches RoundStarted, the second's handler of RoundStarted writes Round started; a slot whose plan's on load dispatches SlotOpened, handled by the slot's own plan and by the page's.
promises.gesture: Open the page, then load the slot.
promises.outcome: The page shows Round started; after the load, both the slot's text and the page's text read Slot opened.
promises.opposite: A dispatch of an event no plan handles changes no text.
promises.defect: On load runs before the second plan or the slot's plan subscribes, so Round started or the slot's Slot opened never shows.

features.summary: An app event: declared once as a static member, raised by a Dispatch step or from markup, and heard by its handlers with its typed payload, a literal or an object built from sources.

meanings.meaning: A dispatch raises its event on the document as a CustomEvent whose detail is the payload in the live form (gate 1's P8), or null when it carries none. The DOM runs the event's listeners inside the dispatch, in the order they subscribed, one listener a handler, so its handlers run across plans in D17.3's order and each runs up to its first awaited step before the step after Dispatch runs (D11.5, Ownership.tla:HandlersHearInTheOrderTheySubscribed); a stop in a handler ends that handler only, and the dispatching pipeline goes on (D4.8). A handler reads its payload as data (D4.2): a member the payload lacks reads its start, and a payload of null reads nothing, so a dispatch with no payload of an event that declares one runs its handlers with every member reading nothing.

Markup raises its event on a click at or inside the element it marks, once per click, with the payload of the innermost marked element that holds the click's target; the core's document plugin listens to clicks once per page, in the capture phase, and reads only its own attributes on the target's ancestors. The payload is one attribute per member, data-alis-detail- and the member's name, holding its text: the form Html.Raises writes where the view renders and a Fusion template's event button fills in the browser, which D15.2 keeps as it is. Html.Raises writes each member as the plan's live form writes it, from the payload the app's JSON contract writes, with no reflection of the core's own: a text as itself, a number as its number, an enum and a date as the live form writes them, a boolean as true or false; a member that holds null is carried by no attribute of its own and is named in one attribute of the core's, data-alis-null, which Html.Raises writes whenever it is given a payload, empty when no member holds null. The document plugin raises a detail of null only from a marked element that carries neither a member attribute nor data-alis-null, markup raised with no payload (M1.D2), and otherwise an object that holds each carried member's text and null for each member data-alis-null names, so a handler reads from markup what it reads from Dispatch of the same payload. A record, a list, and a member whose name is not a lowercase letter followed by letters, digits or underscores, since the browser lowercases an attribute's name, are refused where the view renders, naming Dispatch. The handler of an app event reads each scalar member of its payload through as with the member's shape, so a member markup carried as text reads as its number, boolean, enum or date, and one Dispatch carried in the live form reads as it is.

features.oracle: The DOM Standard: dispatchEvent runs an event's listeners synchronously in the order they were added and reports a listener's exception without stopping the dispatch, a CustomEvent carries its detail, and a click's target's ancestors are its path; the HTML Standard, which lowercases an attribute's name in an HTML document; and the spec itself for the payload's live form (gate 1's P8), its reads (D4.2) and the as conversion (D3.13).

defects.defect: A dispatch's handlers run after the step that follows Dispatch, or a stop in one of them stops the dispatching pipeline, so the dispatcher's next text is written before the handler's or never (M1.D2, D4.8).

A payload built from sources reaches its handler in another shape: a nested member arrives outside its holder, a literal member beside the sources is lost, or a source is read when the page renders rather than when the step runs (M1.D2, N7.1).

Markup raises with the wrong payload or the wrong number of times: a click inside a marked item nested in another raises the outer one's payload or both, a number markup carried as text is read as text, or a click outside every marked element raises one (M1.D3).

Markup that raises a payload holding a record or a list writes it as text or drops it, where it is refused where the view renders with the redesign's message: "Raise a payload that holds a record or a list from a pipeline, with p.Dispatch." (M1.D3).

Markup that raises a member whose name an attribute cannot carry back reaches the handler under a lowercased name that reads nothing, where it is refused where the view renders with the redesign's message: "Rename it, or raise the payload from a pipeline, with p.Dispatch." (M1.D3).
An event that declares a payload, raised with none, stops its handler or shows the members' starts, where each read reads nothing and the handler runs on (M1.D2, D4.2).

Markup hands a handler another payload than Dispatch of the same value: a member that holds null reads its start, or a payload whose members all hold null raises a detail of null, so its members read nothing (M1.D3, D4.2).
Two AppEvent declarations of one event name in one compilation compile, so a handler of one hears the other's dispatch with another payload type: ALIS039, new:M1.N6.

A dispatch whose payload is not its event's payload type, or a handler that reads a member its event's payload does not declare, does not compile: Dispatch takes AppEvent<TPayload> with a TPayload or a TypedSource<TPayload>, and the handler's payload is a Data<TPayload>, M1.N4 and M1.N3.

promises.page: A desk whose button's handler dispatches CallLogged, then copies the pager's text into the desk's status; CallLogged has two handlers: the first sets the log's text to Logged and then reads the Text of a ConformanceComponent at the id absent-scanner, an element the page does not render, which stops it, the second sets the pager's text from Idle to Paged.
promises.outcome: The log reads Logged, the pager reads Paged, and the desk's status reads Paged.
promises.opposite: With no handler of CallLogged, the desk's status copies Idle.
promises.defect: The handlers run after the dispatcher's next step, so the status reads Idle, the first handler's stop ends the dispatch, so the pager keeps Idle, or it ends the dispatcher, so the status keeps its text.

promises.page: A transfer form with a name input and a destination ward input bound to a nested member, whose button dispatches Transfer built from both with the reason literal fall; the handler shows the name, the destination's ward and the reason.
promises.gesture: Type Ada and East, click the button, then change the ward to West and click again.
promises.outcome: The handler shows Ada, East and fall, then Ada, West and fall.
promises.opposite: With the ward input left empty, the ward's text shows nothing and the name still shows Ada.
promises.defect: The ward arrives outside its destination so its text shows nothing, fall is lost beside the sources, or the second click shows East again.

promises.page: A visitor list whose item raises Announced with party size 12, the gate's capacity 9 and the type a coach party, the item holding a nested button that raises Announced with party size 1, capacity 9 and the type a visitor, and a paragraph outside every item; the handler shows the type, the party size, and Over capacity when the party size is greater than the capacity, else Within capacity.
promises.gesture: Click the nested button, then the item around it, then the paragraph.
promises.outcome: After the first click the handler shows a visitor, 1 and Within capacity; after the second it shows a coach party, 12 and Over capacity; after the third it still shows a coach party, 12 and Over capacity.
promises.opposite: An item raised with party size 4 and capacity 9 shows Within capacity.
promises.defect: The nested click raises the outer item's payload or raises twice, the two numbers are read as the texts 12 and 9 and compare 12 below 9 so Over capacity never shows, or the paragraph's click raises an event.

promises.page: A gate whose bell button raises Announced with no payload; its handler writes the party size's text, then writes Rung.
promises.outcome: The party size's text is empty and the status reads Rung.
promises.opposite: Raised with party size 3, the party size's text reads 3.
promises.defect: The missing payload stops the handler, so Rung never shows, or its party size reads its start and shows 0.

promises.page: An escort desk whose handler of an escort request, whose Guide starts as the porter and whose Note starts null, shows No guide when the guide IsNull, else the guide; three buttons raise it from markup, one with the guide null and the note Late, one with both null, and one with no payload, and a fourth raises the first button's payload with Dispatch.
promises.gesture: Click the four buttons in turn, reading the guide text after each.
promises.outcome: The first, second and fourth clicks show No guide; the third empties the guide text.
promises.opposite: Raised from markup with the guide Ruth, the guide text shows Ruth.
promises.defect: Markup carries the null guide by no attribute, so the first click reads its start and shows the porter where Dispatch shows No guide, or the payload whose members all hold null raises null, so the second click empties the text.

promises.page: A gate whose visitor item raises Announced with an escort record beside its party size.
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with one error naming the escort member and Dispatch, and no gate renders.
promises.opposite: The same item raising only a party size and a type renders, and its click raises Announced.
promises.defect: The record is written as the text [object Object] or dropped, so the page renders and the handler reads a wrong escort or nothing.

promises.page: A signed visit whose markup raises a payload member the app names VisitorName by its JsonPropertyName.
promises.outcome: The page is refused where the view renders with one error naming the member, its name VisitorName, and Dispatch.
promises.opposite: The same member named visitorName renders, and a click shows the visitor's name.
promises.defect: The browser lowercases the attribute's name, so the page renders and the handler reads nothing for VisitorName.
